Often heard more than seen along undersea cliffs, billowing clouds of grit obscure several vortautili that slam and grind into stone to 
dislodge barnacles and clams, grasping them in their black tentacles. With adaptations to survive the frigid depths and migrations to 
colder climes, the vortautilus’ is suffused with an ethanol-like fluids that allows them to function in waters that most other aquatic 
life would suffer a slow torpor. Th ese cephalopod take advantage of the lack in competition during the colder seasons. When sheets of 
ice begin to form in the depths of winter, resonating deep cracking sounds are often heard as they spin violently into the ice sheets, 
creating new waterways to search for their favored prey, or, as the new year dawns, slamming in bouts of contending for mates.

Water Breathing Th e vortautilus can breathe only water, With the 
use of its chambered shell, it may hold its breath for 1 hour.
Curling Shell Th e vortautilus can retract or emerge from its shell 
as an Action. While retracted, it gains +2 bonus to AC (total 18) 
and cannot use the Gripping Tentacles or Spiral Vortex attacks but 
it may use its Th ermal Torrent and Jet Siphon. 
Digging Spiral Th e vortautilus can burrow through solid earth 
and ice at a speed of 5 ft. leaving behind a 3 ft. wide tunnel.
Spinning Shoal When the vortautilus moves and performs a 
Spiral Vortex Attack towards a target creature, any allied vortautili 
that are within 30 ft. and can see the target creature may use their 
Bonus Action to move up to their speed towards the same target 
creature and make a Spiral Vortex Attack as well.

Encountering Found in hunting groups of several individuals, 
the vortautilus are often obscured in billowing clouds of sand 
and debris as they break and tear at the ocean floor looking 
for clams and urchins to feast on. Naturally curious, they will 
approach a Traveler if they offer a soft fleshed starfi sh for them 
to snatch into their many grasping tentacles, but will attack in 
unison if threatened.
Creature Collaborator • CAPT Splashclaw
The inversed spiral shell is comprised of a nacreous 
structure of numerous layered platelets of calcium 
carbonate that reinforce it beyond what many other 
shelled creatures could ever hope to achieve
Dozens of dark inky tentacles coil outwards from the 
cephalopod’s head. While lacking suction cups, they 
harbor a powerful grip, capable of constricting and 
breaking rock-hard barnacles and large crustaceans 
with ease
Primitive single chamber 
eyes swivel on thick stalks 
to collect the meager light 
in the depths. As they lack a 
lens, they instead rely more 
heavily on their olfactory 
senses and can locate prey 
even in the darkest recesses
